agent_explanations_oldest_first.text: The gain has two sources. The edited model loops far less (finished answers rise from 187 to 246 of 256), and it is more accurate on the answers it finishes (24.1% → 28.9%). The wrong→right example shows the pattern. The original spirals into a loop with absurd numbers ("$45000000 * 3"), while the edited model solves the problem in two clean steps. So head 3 of layer 11 drives both runaway looping and worse reasoning in eval-format math. Next is the strength test. E10 = E4 + head 3's o_proj columns × −0.5, a partial reversal, on the same dev_b[:256]. If reversal beats zeroing, the head's contribution acts as a pure suppressor and the effect is monotone along it. If it is clearly worse than E9, zero is near the optimum (as with the neurons, where reversal hurt), and I'll keep removal and look for a narrower version of it.
E10 is saved: E4 plus head 3's output reversed at half strength. I'll run the paired generation on dev_b[:256] and compare it with E9's +9.0 on the same problems.

The strength series turns out non-monotone. Original weight (1): 18.75%. Zero: 27.7% (+9.0). Reversal at −0.5: 10.2% (−8.6, 11 wrong→right, 33 right→wrong), with almost no loops but many short wrong answers. So head 3 mixes two things: a component that causes looping and suppression, and a useful component the model needs for correct reasoning. Zeroing removes both, and reversing destroys the useful part. A narrower edit that removes only the harmful part should do better than E9. My working hypothesis, from fwd_12/fwd_19, is that the harmful part is what head 3 reads from the chat-template tokens, the source of the eval-format gate. Step 1 is to check in fwd_12 (attention for 2 texts at layers 5, 11, 17 and 23) exactly which token positions L11 head 3 attends to from response queries, grouped by token string. The share falling on template tokens such as "<start_of_turn>", "user", "model" and "<end_of_turn>" tells me which tokens' value vectors to target. A large share on a few template tokens would support a value-subspace edit. Attention spread over the problem text would make that edit unattractive.

fwd_12 holds L11 attention for 2 texts (167 tokens): the add2 probe and a v0 reference solution, both in eval chat format. For each text I'll locate the response start (after "<start_of_turn>model\n") and average head 3's attention over response queries. I'll then report the mass on BOS, template tokens, problem text, prompt suffix and earlier response tokens, plus the top key positions by mass with short benign token strings. Heads 0–2 serve as a comparison.
